cards.text: Meet Solomon, and the first thing we hear is a BIG move. He forms an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. He brings her to the City of David until he finishes his palace, the house of the LORD and the wall around Jerusalem.
But here's the catch. The people are still sacrificing on the high places.

cards.question: Why are the people still sacrificing on the high places?

answers.text: No house for the LORD's Name was built yet
The king ordered them to go there

cards.text: Now, Solomon himself. He walks in the statutes of his father David.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon loved the LORD.
Solomon walked in his father David's statutes, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the ___.

cards.text: So the king heads to Gibeon, the great high place, and offers a THOUSAND burnt offerings on the altar there. Friend, I stamped forty cookies in a row once and had to go lie down on my gold base.
Then one night at Gibeon, the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream.

cards.question: In the dream at Gibeon, what does God say to Solomon?

answers.text: Ask and I will give it to you
Go and build My house for Me
Rise and lead My people out

cards.text: Before Solomon asks for anything, he looks back at his father David. He says God showed David much loving devotion.

cards.question: Why does Solomon say God showed his father David so much loving devotion?

answers.text: David won every battle he fought

cards.text: And God kept that devotion going by giving David a son to sit on his throne this very day. That son is Solomon, made king in his father's place.
But Solomon says he's only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in. That's day one as the BOSS, holding the keys to the whole building, and you can't even find the light switch.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon tells God he already knows how to lead.
Solomon says he's among the people God has chosen. He says they're too ___ to count or number.
God said ask. So what does Solomon ask God to give him?

answers.text: A heart to judge with understanding
Wealth to build a great kingdom

cards.question: Solomon wants to judge God's people and discern between good and evil. True or false: he says he needs help because the people refuse to obey him.

cards.text: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon asked for this. Me? I'd have asked for an oven that never burns a batch, and called it a prayer request.
So God answers him, starting with what Solomon DIDN'T ask for. Not long life, and not wealth for himself.

cards.question: Besides long life and wealth, what else does God say Solomon didn't ask for?
God says He'll do what Solomon asked and give him a wise and ___ heart.
True or false: God says there will never have been another like Solomon, and there never will be.

cards.text: Then God keeps going. He's about to give Solomon something he never requested.

cards.question: What does God give Solomon on top of what he asked for?

cards.text: Riches AND honor, with no man in any kingdom his equal all his days. That's like asking for one cookie and walking out with the bakery, the ovens AND the delivery cart.

cards.question: God adds one promise with an if. If Solomon walks in God's ways like David did, God says, "I will ___ your days."

cards.text: Then Solomon wakes up, and sure enough, it had been a dream. The best dream I ever had was a cookie box that packed itself, and I woke up hugging my own mustache.

cards.question: Solomon wakes up at Gibeon. True or false: he heads back to Jerusalem.

cards.text: In Jerusalem, Solomon stands before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. He offers burnt offerings and peace offerings.

cards.question: After his offerings before the ark, how does Solomon wrap it all up?

answers.text: He holds a feast for his servants
He builds a new altar at Gibeon
He writes a song for the people

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "I will ___ your days.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Solomon is introduced only with "Meet Solomon." The opening never says simply who he is, such as Israel's king.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 13 has already said that Solomon does not know how to go out or come in. That directly gives away the answer to card 14, which asks whether Solomon says he already knows how to lead.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Cards 3, 5, 11 and 13 provide no preceding setup from which their answers can be reasoned: the third thing Solomon did not request, God's uniqueness promise, Solomon's return to Jerusalem and his closing feast. Four of the stop's seven choice cards are therefore discovery questions, so informed guesses do not make up most of the stop.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
